subject.title: [Bug]: Discord routing / mention-gating issue in OpenClaw

question: Should Discord preflight implement single active-target suppression for configured bots/agents, and should role mentions and plain-text agent-name delegation participate in that target decision?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but changing active-target precedence, role semantics, quoted-text scoping, and bot-authored message handling can intentionally suppress messages in existing multi-agent Discord setups.

options.title: Adopt active-target suppression
options.body: Implement Discord-owned target selection before default admission using configured bot/account/agent metadata, with explicit current-bot mentions allowed and other configured targets suppressed.

options.title: Split the policy work
options.body: Let #13487 own native mention/reply/default-owner precedence while keeping this issue for quoted-text, role, and bot-authored residual cases.

options.title: Defer fuzzy signals
options.body: Fix only native Discord mention/reply metadata now and leave role-label and plain-text delegation semantics to separate product work.

recommendation.title: Adopt active-target suppression
recommendation.body: Implement Discord-owned target selection before default admission using configured bot/account/agent metadata, with explicit current-bot mentions allowed and other configured targets suppressed.

likelyOwner.reason: The current shared mention decision shape and recent Discord preflight refactors trace most clearly to steipete's commits.
